open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-91 blocking
open_points.text: Whether any value it holds — a customer's contact or fiscal data, an object's address — must be blocked after erasure rather than erased is a question for the legal review of the governance
open_points.question: Which Registry values require blocking, when does blocking begin, how long does it last, who may access blocked values, and what exact action destroys them when it ends?
options: Registry never stores blocked values and erases every affected value
Registry blocks specified fields inside their existing records
Registry moves specified values to a separate blocked store
open_points.default_guess: Keep the stated interim behavior: erase in Registry until a new owner decision defines blocking.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-92 trace correlation
open_points.text: Whether Kernel writes the key it gives as that request id into its trace record, so that a room or pointer leads to exactly one node execution, is Kernel's to state in its case; until it does, the link is one-directional.
open_points.question: Must Kernel record Registry's request id as a unique searchable correlation key, and what uniqueness, retry and cardinality rules bind that key?
options: One request id identifies exactly one Kernel node execution
One request id may identify several retry executions of one logical node
Kernel need not store the request id, leaving only one-directional correlation
open_points.default_guess: Require one logical node execution per request id while allowing its retry attempts to share that correlation key.

witness.initial: A pointer stores the publisher, session and publish request id, while Kernel's trace schema has not been decided.
events: An agent publishes a pointer through a Kernel node.
The owner starts from the stored pointer and tries to find the execution that produced it.
outcomes: Kernel recorded the request id, so exactly one logical execution is found.
Kernel did not record the request id, so the stored pointer cannot be correlated deterministically.
witness.observer: The owner investigating the agent's action

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-92 withdrawal trace link
open_points.text: the request id a room's create carries (State 1 M03) and the publisher, with its session, and the request id of a pointer's publish
open_points.question: What Registry fact, if any, links a pointer withdrawal to the Kernel execution that performed it?
options: Store the withdrawal request id, publisher and session on the pointer history
Link withdrawals only through Registry's audit log
Store no Registry-side link and search Kernel's trace by time and operation
open_points.default_guess: Store a withdrawal request id, publisher and session alongside the withdrawal event.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-93 duplicate customer records
open_points.text: 'read a customer'; 'list projects' with the archived ones, whose items carry `customer_ref`, to find the projects that name the customer
open_points.question: How does the owner find every Customer record and project about one data subject when recording the same person twice is allowed to create two unrelated Customer identities?
options: The owner searches and manually matches all customer records by personal fields
Registry supplies a subject-level search or matching operation
Each request covers only the single Customer identity selected by the owner
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to search all Customer records by the supplied identifiers and include every credible match.

witness.initial: The same person has two Customer records with different `customer_ref` values and projects under both.
events: The person submits an access request.
The owner selects one Customer record and follows R0-93's reads from that record.
outcomes: Only projects naming the selected `customer_ref` are returned.
Both Customer records and all their projects are returned after an additional identity-matching process.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-93 machine-readable answer
open_points.text: The machine-readable copy is the owner's, assembled from those reads.
open_points.question: What records and fields must the copy contain, in what machine-readable format and schema, and how are absent, restricted, erased, retained or unreadable parts represented?
options: A documented JSON package containing every Registry field found by the procedure
Raw responses from each Registry read without a combined schema
A governance-defined export whose format is outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Produce a versioned JSON object containing the customer, all matched projects, objects, rooms and artifact metadata, with explicit status for omitted or unavailable values.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-93 post-release operation
open_points.text: A read-only owner operation that gathers a customer with every project naming it, as one page and a JSON download, is a candidate change once the first release is assembled; adopting it is a new owner decision here.
open_points.question: Is the combined page and JSON-download operation part of the product, and if so what are its authorization, selection, output and failure semantics?
options: Add it in the release following the first assembly
Include it in the first release
Do not add it; retain the manual governance procedure
open_points.default_guess: Do not implement the candidate until an owner decision adopts and specifies it.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-94 retention configuration
open_points.text: periods the owner sets in the configuration from the schedule
open_points.question: Which period keys, units, allowed values and defaults exist, what happens when a required period is missing or invalid, and when does a changed period take effect?
options: Require validated periods for every review category before Registry starts
Use built-in provisional defaults with optional owner overrides
Omit categories whose period is absent or invalid
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit validated day-based periods for customer relationships, archived projects and audit entries, refusing invalid configuration at startup.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-94 retention review page
open_points.text: it gains a read-only review page in the owner interface: the customers whose relationship ended, and the archived projects archived, longer ago than periods the owner sets in the configuration from the schedule
open_points.question: Does the page include already erased or anonymised records, restricted customers, records currently covered by a lawful retention ground, and records exactly on the deadline; what information and failure state does it show?
options: Show every record past the computed date, including already acted-on records
Show only records past the date that still contain data on which an existing action can operate
Show all past-date records but mark their current disposition and applicable action
open_points.default_guess: Show all past-date records with their disposition, due date and available action, treating a record as due when its deadline is at or before today.

witness.initial: A relationship ended more than its configured period ago, and its contact and fiscal data have already been erased.
events: The owner signs in and opens the retention review page.
outcomes: The erased Customer remains listed because its relationship date is overdue.
The Customer is omitted because there is no remaining personal value to erase.
witness.observer: The owner performing the periodic review

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-94 blocking mechanism
open_points.text: If the legal review answers that some value must be blocked, blocking enters the same change, as one mechanism with the review page. The design of both is decided then, by a new owner decision here.
open_points.question: What blocking state, transitions, permissions, review-page behavior, audit behavior and terminal destruction action will be implemented if the legal review requires blocking?
options: Add a blocked state to existing records
Move blocked values into an isolated store
Keep blocking entirely outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Make no blocking implementation until the required owner decision is recorded.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-95 recipient follow-up
open_points.text: What still holds a value is followed by the owner, by the governance's procedure, after each such change
open_points.question: What identifies every affected recipient, issued document, offline projection and legacy copy after a rectification, restriction or erasure, and what records that each required correction or notification was completed or lawfully omitted?
options: Governance maintains a per-disclosure recipient and copy register with completion records
Each service exposes its own search and correction workflow
The owner relies on manual knowledge without a complete register
open_points.default_guess: Use a governance-held per-disclosure register that names the recipient, copy, owning service, lawful ground and follow-up status.

witness.initial: A customer's erroneous address appears in two issued documents and one legacy service copy.
events: The owner corrects the address in Registry.
The owner follows the governance procedure after the change.
outcomes: A register identifies all three copies and their required corrective actions.
The owner knows of only two copies, leaving the third unchanged.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-96 special-category data
open_points.text: data of a special category (GDPR Art. 9), which the platform must not hand to an agent. ... Registry cannot tell what a word means, refuses no name for its content and searches no text for words; a name that breaks the rule does reach the agent.
open_points.question: Is preventing special-category data from reaching the agent a guaranteed system behavior or only a writer obligation whose violation the system accepts and transmits?
options: Guarantee prevention with validation or human approval before disclosure
Treat it only as a governance rule and withdraw the unconditional platform guarantee
Accept the value but quarantine it from the agent until the owner classifies it
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a governance rule rather than a technical guarantee unless an enforceable review step is added.

witness.initial: A project is granted to an agent session and has no prohibited room name yet.
events: The owner or agent adds a room named "bathroom for the wheelchair".
The agent reads the project projection.
outcomes: The platform must not hand the special-category implication to the agent.
Registry accepts the name and returns it to the agent.
witness.observer: The agent, its AI provider and the affected customer

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-96 writer guidance
open_points.text: That description is changed with the changes planned after the first release is assembled (R0-93, R0-94); until then the rule binds the owner, and the agent through the governance's instructions to it.
open_points.question: Before the manifest and owner-interface descriptions are changed, what concrete component supplies the rule to every agent and owner writing a room name or alias, and what happens if those instructions are absent or stale?
options: Update the manifest and owner interface before any such write is enabled
Kernel injects a versioned governance instruction into every relevant agent run
Rely on the owner and agent remembering an external governance document
open_points.default_guess: Update the manifest descriptions and owner-interface guidance before enabling the affected writes.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-97 refused-attempt counters
open_points.text: Registry counts refused attempts in memory from its start and shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in, with the instant of the start and of the latest of each kind
open_points.question: What is one attempt, how are requests matching several kinds classified, whether a lockout is counted once or per refused request, and whether concurrent attempts must update the count atomically?
options: Use mutually exclusive precedence-ordered categories and count each HTTP request once
Increment every applicable category for one request
Count security events rather than requests, with lockout as a separate event
open_points.default_guess: Define mutually exclusive precedence-ordered categories, count each refused HTTP request once, and count entry into lockout as its own event.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-97 locked-out owner visibility
open_points.text: shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in
open_points.question: How can the owner learn that a lockout caused sign-in refusal while the owner remains unable to sign in, and what observable failure distinguishes lockout from a wrong credential?
options: Show a non-sensitive lockout indication on the refused sign-in page
Reveal the cause only after a later successful sign-in
Provide a separate owner-only operational status channel
open_points.default_guess: Keep the public refusal indistinguishable, then show the lockout count and latest time immediately after the next successful sign-in.

witness.initial: Repeated attempts have locked the owner credential, and the counters contain the lockout.
events: The legitimate owner tries to sign in while the lockout remains active.
outcomes: The owner sees only a generic refusal and cannot know why sign-in failed.
The sign-in response identifies the lockout or exposes another status path.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-97 post-release delivery
open_points.text: After the first release is assembled, with the changes R0-93, R0-94 and R0-96 planned, Registry counts refused attempts in memory
open_points.question: Which release must introduce the counters and sign-in display, and may production operate after the first release without this measure?
options: The first release may operate without counters until a later specified release
Counters are required before the first production release
Counters are required immediately in the next release after assembly
open_points.default_guess: Require the counters in the next release and explicitly record the first release as lacking them until upgraded.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-98 DPIA determination
open_points.text: On these facts the screening's likely conclusion is that a DPIA is not required
open_points.question: What is the actual screening decision, who records it, and what happens to production start and import if the screening instead concludes that a DPIA is required?
options: Conclude now that no DPIA is required and record the reasons
Require a completed DPIA before production start or import
Allow start and import while completing any required DPIA in parallel
open_points.default_guess: Record a final screening decision before production use; if it requires a DPIA, complete that assessment before the newly designed processing begins.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-98 cleanup ordering
open_points.text: It holds once the owner's earlier machine no longer gives the agent the objects folder (the cleanup step of the home server's move). ... Registry's production start and its one import (R0-79) do not wait for the screening
open_points.question: Must production start or import wait for removal of the agent's access to the earlier objects folder, and what verifies that the cleanup succeeded?
options: Cleanup and verification are prerequisites to production start and import
Import may proceed, but agent-facing processing waits for verified cleanup
Everything may proceed in parallel despite the screening premise not yet holding
open_points.default_guess: Make verified removal of the agent's old objects-folder access a prerequisite to agent-facing production processing.

witness.initial: The earlier machine still lets the agent read the objects folder.
events: The owner starts production Registry and imports the VPS projects before completing cleanup.
An agent continues running on the earlier machine.
outcomes: The claimed screening facts do not yet hold because the agent can still read home photos.
The import is treated as safe and processing continues without waiting for cleanup.
witness.observer: The owner conducting the DPIA screening and any person visible in the photos

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-98 agent document intake
open_points.text: That the agent reads these documents from a folder of its own, holding them alone, is a change of the platform outside this case.
open_points.question: Who creates and controls that folder, how documents reach it without prohibited customer names or delivery addresses, what validates or reviews them, and what happens when a prohibited value is present?
options: The owner manually reviews and places sanitized documents in the folder
A trusted service sanitizes documents before agent access
The agent receives original documents and relies only on governance instructions
open_points.default_guess: Require owner review and deliberate placement into an agent-only input folder, rejecting documents containing customer names or delivery addresses.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-99 exact approval
open_points.text: Each such write of the agent waits for the owner's approval of its exact request, unless the owner gave that flow version a standing approval for the node
open_points.question: Which request fields, project and session identities, flow and node versions, request id, and displayed values are bound by an exact approval, and which change invalidates it?
options: Bind approval to the canonical complete request plus session, project, flow version and node version
Bind it only to the flow and node version
Bind it to the displayed business fields but not transport metadata
open_points.default_guess: Bind approval cryptographically to the canonical full request, project, session, operation, flow version and node version; any change requires new approval.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-99 standing approvals in maps
open_points.text: The governance's rule is that no standing approval is given to a node that writes to Registry inside a map over a collection.
open_points.question: Which component detects that a Registry-writing node is inside a map and prevents or refuses the standing approval, and what observable failure occurs when one is attempted?
options: Kernel enforces the prohibition when standing approval is created or used
The owner interface refuses such approval after inspecting the flow graph
It is an unenforced governance instruction to the owner
open_points.default_guess: Have Kernel reject creation and use of a standing approval for a Registry-writing node reachable inside a collection map.

witness.initial: A flow contains a Registry room-create node inside a map over an arbitrary collection.
events: The owner attempts to give that node standing approval.
The flow runs over one thousand items.
outcomes: An enforcing component refuses the standing approval, so every write requires an exact approval.
The governance rule is advisory, the standing approval is accepted, and one run creates one thousand rooms.
witness.observer: The owner and every consumer of the project

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions — R0-99 future write limits
open_points.text: A count enforced by Registry is reconsidered, by a new owner decision here, if standing approvals for such writes become needed.
open_points.question: What condition establishes that standing approvals are needed, what room, pointer and request limits would apply, and is enabling such approvals forbidden until those limits are decided?
options: Forbid the standing approvals unless a prior owner decision adds limits
Permit them without limits and reconsider only after observed harm
Define conservative limits now
open_points.default_guess: Forbid standing approval for mapped Registry writes until a new owner decision defines enforceable limits.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Explicit exclusions — governance boundary
open_points.text: blocking under LOPDGDD Art. 32 (R0-91), the procedure that answers a data subject's request (R0-93), incident response and the other organisational measures
open_points.question: Which named governance owner and artifact supplies these procedures to Registry's owner, how Registry-version changes are synchronized with them, and what blocks release when a required procedure is absent?
options: A versioned platform-governance package is a release prerequisite
Unversioned external documents are maintained independently
No governance artifact is required for a Registry release
open_points.default_guess: Require a named, versioned governance package and checklist as a production-release prerequisite.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Open questions — unresolved R0-91 to R0-99 choices
open_points.text: None open. ... R0-91 to R0-99 (2026-11-23) answer Q1 to Q9 of the data-protection requirements matrix.
open_points.question: Where are the expressly deferred legal, product, trace-correlation, blocking, post-release and DPIA decisions tracked if this unit declares that no question remains open?
options: List every deferred decision in Open questions
Declare each deferred matter an explicit exclusion with a named receiving specification
Decide every matter in State 0 before closing it
open_points.default_guess: List the unresolved decisions as open questions with owners, dependencies and closure criteria.
